questions.question: A hundredths grid is made of 100 equal small squares, and the whole grid is 1 whole. Maya colours 7 of the squares blue. Which decimal shows the blue part of the grid?
questions.explain: 7 shaded out of 100 squares is 7/100, and hundredths need two places after the decimal point, so it is 0.07. The common trap is writing 0.7, which is 7 tenths — that would be 70 shaded squares, not 7.

questions.question: A hundredths grid has 100 equal squares and stands for 1 whole. Exactly 40 squares are shaded green. Which line writes the green part correctly as a percent, a decimal and a fraction?
questions.explain: 40 out of 100 is 40%, which is 40/100 = 0.4, and 40/100 simplifies to 2/5 by dividing top and bottom by 20. Watch the decimal point: 40/100 is 0.4 (forty hundredths), not 0.04 or 4.0.

questions.question: A hundredths grid has 100 equal squares in 10 rows of 10, and the whole grid is 1 whole. Three full rows are shaded, plus 5 extra squares in the next row. What percent of the grid is shaded, and what is that as a decimal?
questions.explain: Three full rows are 30 squares plus 5 more makes 35 out of 100, so 35% = 35/100 = 0.35. The trap is sliding the decimal point the wrong number of places — hundredths always need exactly two decimal places.

questions.question: A hundredths grid has 100 equal squares and the whole grid stands for 1 whole. Ren shades squares until the shaded part is exactly 0.9 of the grid. How many squares are shaded, and what percent is that?
questions.explain: 0.9 means 9 tenths, and 9 tenths is the same as 90 hundredths, so 90 of the 100 squares are shaded and that is 90%. The trap is reading 0.9 as 9 hundredths and shading only 9 squares.

questions.question: Write 6% as a decimal.
questions.explain: Percent means out of 100, so 6% = 6/100, and 6 hundredths is written with two decimal places: 0.06. The most common mistake is moving the decimal point only one place and writing 0.6, which is really 60%.

questions.question: A sign in a Nanaimo bookstore says 3/20 off every comic. What percent off is that?
questions.explain: Make an equivalent fraction with denominator 100: multiply numerator and denominator of 3/20 by 5 to get 15/100, which is 15%. Two traps here — adding 3 + 20 to get 23, and shifting the decimal point to land on 1.5%.

questions.question: A weather app says 0.45 of the days last month were rainy. Which pair shows that same amount as a percent and as a fraction?
questions.explain: 0.45 is 45 hundredths, so it is 45/100, which is exactly 45%. The trap is moving the decimal point the wrong number of places and getting 4.5% or 0.45% — hundredths and percents line up two places apart.

questions.question: Which fraction is equal to 35%?
questions.explain: 35% means 35 out of 100, and 35/100 divides by 5 on the top and bottom to give 7/20. Check any answer by building it back up to hundredths: 7/25 is 28/100 = 28%, so it does not fit.

questions.question: A skateboard shop in Kelowna advertises 5% off. Ravi wants to find the discount on a $60 board, so he enters 60 x 0.5 on his calculator and gets $30 off. Which statement explains what went wrong?
options: 5% means 5 out of 100 = 0.05, so he should multiply by 0.05 — he moved the decimal only one place
5% = 0.5, because you drop the percent sign and put a decimal in front, so the discount really is $30
5% = 5.0, because the percent sign just means the number 5, so he should have multiplied by 5 to get $300
5% = 0.005, because a percent needs the decimal point moved three places, so he should have used 0.005
questions.explain: Percent means parts per hundred, so 5% = 5/100 = 0.05 and the discount is 60 x 0.05 = $3. Using 0.5 turns 5% into 50%, which is why the answer came out ten times too big.

questions.question: Four stores in the same Burnaby mall advertise their sale on the same $50 backpack. Sport Shack says 1/4 off, Wheels West says 15% off, Board Barn says 3/10 off, and Ride On says 0.35 off. Which store gives the biggest discount?
questions.explain: Change every sign into a percent first: 1/4 = 25/100 = 25%, 3/10 = 30/100 = 30%, and 0.35 = 35/100 = 35%, so 0.35 off is the largest. The trap is misreading 0.35 as 3.5% and picking the 3/10 sign instead.

questions.question: One sign in a Victoria shop says 0.25 off and another sign next door says 1/4 off. Ling says both signs mean the same discount. Is she right?
options: No — 0.25 off means 2.5% off, so 1/4 off is the better deal
No — 0.25 off is 25% off but 1/4 off is only 4% off
Yes — 0.25 = 25/100 = 1/4, so both signs mean 25% off
No — 0.25 off is 25% off but 1/4 off is only 14% off
questions.explain: Turn both into hundredths: 0.25 is 25 hundredths = 25/100, and 1/4 becomes 25/100 when you multiply top and bottom by 25, so both are 25%. Two traps to avoid — reading 0.25 as 2.5% and grabbing the denominator 4 to call it 4%.

questions.question: During Bike to School Week, 4 out of every 5 students in Mr. Chan’s class rode or walked. He wants that written as a percent and as a decimal for the school newsletter. Which pair is correct?
questions.explain: Build an equivalent fraction with 100 on the bottom: 4/5 times 20/20 gives 80/100, which is 80% and 0.8 as a decimal. The trap is writing 0.08, which is only 8 hundredths — that would be 8%, not 80%.
